name: San Diego
operatingHours: San Diego Trolley runs ~4:30 AM–~1:00 AM daily, every 7.5–15 min by day and every 15–30 min early and late. There is no all-night trolley service.
fareInfo: From Oct 1, 2026 an adult one-way trolley or bus ride is $3, including 2 hours of transfers; a day pass is ~$7. Pay with the PRONTO card or app (which caps at the day-pass price); contactless bank cards are accepted but don't cap. The airport bus (Route 992) costs the regular $3 fare.

sights.name: San Diego Zoo
sights.note: A huge hillside zoo in Balboa Park, known for its pandas, gorillas and koalas; the Skyfari aerial tram and guided bus tour help cover the ground.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily (later in summer and holidays)

sights.name: USS Midway Museum
sights.note: A decommissioned aircraft carrier moored on the downtown waterfront, with restored jets on the flight deck and veteran docents below.

sights.name: La Jolla Cove
sights.note: A small sheltered cove below sandstone cliffs where sea lions and seals haul out and snorkelers find garibaldi fish in clear water.

sights.name: Balboa Park
sights.note: A 1,200-acre park of Spanish Revival pavilions, gardens and 17 museums strung along the pedestrian El Prado.
sights.hours: Grounds open 24 hours; most museums ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM (varies, some closed Mon)

sights.name: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve
sights.note: Clifftop trails through rare Torrey pines with long views over the Pacific and down to the beach.

sights.name: Sunset Cliffs Natural Park
sights.note: Eroded sandstone bluffs and sea arches along Point Loma's west edge, the classic spot to watch the sun go down.
sights.hours: Open daily; best at sunset (stay back from crumbling edges)

sights.name: Petco Park
sights.note: The Padres' ballpark in the East Village, with a grassy park beyond the outfield and the Western Metal building built into the stands.
sights.hours: Game and event days; ballpark tours most non-game days

sights.name: La Jolla Shores Park
sights.note: A wide, gentle sandy beach and lawn, popular for families, beginner surfers and kayak trips to the sea caves.

sights.name: Cabrillo National Monument
sights.note: The tip of Point Loma, with a 19th-century lighthouse, sweeping bay views and tide pools at low tide.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily; entry fee per vehicle or walker

sights.name: Birch Aquarium at Scripps
sights.note: Scripps Institution of Oceanography's public aquarium, with a kelp-forest tank, seahorses and an ocean-view tide-pool plaza.

sights.name: Pacific Beach
sights.note: A lively surf beach centred on Crystal Pier, with a busy boardwalk of taco shops, bars and bike rentals.

sights.name: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
sights.note: Restored adobes and 1800s buildings around a grassy plaza marking where California's first European settlement grew, with free museums and Mexican restaurants nearby.
sights.hours: Grounds open daily; museums ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM

sights.name: Mission Beach Boardwalk
sights.note: A three-mile beachfront promenade for walking, skating and cycling, passing the vintage Giant Dipper roller coaster at Belmont Park.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; Belmont Park rides from ~11:00 AM

sights.name: Mt. Soledad National Veterans Memorial
sights.note: A hilltop memorial cross ringed by plaques, with one of the best free 360-degree views over La Jolla and the coast.

sights.name: Coronado Beach
sights.note: A broad, glittering beach in front of the turreted Hotel del Coronado, reached by the bay ferry from downtown's Broadway Pier.

sights.name: Liberty Public Market
sights.note: A food hall in a former Navy training-center building at Liberty Station, with dozens of stalls from tacos to fresh pasta.

railStations.name: Santa Fe Depot
railStations.note: Downtown's 1915 Mission Revival station: Amtrak Pacific Surfliner to Los Angeles and Santa Barbara, and COASTER commuter trains to Oceanside. Trolley Blue and Green lines stop outside; airport bus 992 leaves a block away at Broadway & Kettner.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:30 AM–~midnight; trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: San Diego International Airport
airports.transitNote: Not on the trolley map. MTS bus 992 runs from Terminals 1 and 2 to downtown (Santa Fe Depot / Broadway) every 15 min in ~15 min for $3. The free San Diego Flyer shuttle links both terminals with the trolley and COASTER at Old Town Transit Center every 20–30 min.
airports.hours: Route 992 ~4:00 AM–midnight daily; trolley at Santa Fe Depot ~4:30 AM–~1:00 AM.
